findings.title: Possible TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. Several callers now pass `[]` (cron, webhook, confirm and others), and handleNewBooking can pass `null`. Any Google Meet booking with no destination calendar will throw instead of falling back to Cal Video. The old code used `?.`. It needs `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Pushing team destination calendars onto a null array, and wrong main destination
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so collective team members' calendars are silently dropped. This is the exact scenario the PR is meant to fix. Also, when the event type has a destinationCalendar it is placed first, which is correct. But the organizer's own calendar is then never added in that case, so the organizer is not invited. The array should be built explicitly, e.g. `[]` plus organizer plus team members.

findings.title: loadUsers rewrite drops organization select and changes behavior
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` removes the `organization: { select: { slug } }` from the dynamic user query, so downstream code that reads `user.organization` may break or silently lose data. It also now throws 'dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty' for any request without an eventTypeId and an empty list. Other errors are wrapped as a generic HTTP 500. This refactor is unrelated to the PR and risks regressions.

findings.title: Same event created on every team member's credential with the same event object; the else branch lacks externalId
findings.body: In the no-credentialId branch, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without `destination.externalId`. The resulting references therefore carry `externalCalendarId` undefined. On reschedule or cancel, the update/delete then falls back to the default calendar instead of the intended one. Also, because `calEvent.additionalNotes` is mutated in `createEvent` when hideCalendarNotes is set, and the same `event` is shared across all iterations, there are side-effect risks.

findings.title: Organizer attendee email and calendar selection use the first destination for all hosts
findings.body: `createEvent` sets the organizer attendee email from `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` regardless of which credential/calendar is being written. For a second host's calendar the event is created with the first host's calendar email as the organizer. The selected calendar is looked up by `credentialId` only, so if two destinations share a credential the first match always wins.

findings.title: Nonsensical fallback lookup in updateEvent/deleteEvent
findings.body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is dead logic. In the else branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the find compares externalId to a falsy value and will essentially never match. Previously the code fell back to the destination calendar's externalId. Now it falls back to undefined/primary, which is a regression for the fallback case.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation repeats deletes inside the per-reference loop
findings.body: The recurring-events branch iterates over all user calendar credentials and deletes all updated bookings' first calendar reference. This runs once per calendar reference of the booking, which is now several for collective events. That causes duplicate delete calls and wasted API requests, and the single `bookingRef` lookup via `find` still only handles the first calendar reference per updated booking, so multi-host recurring events are not fully cleaned up.

findings.title: Booking only connects to the first destination calendar
findings.body: The booking's `destinationCalendar` relation connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`. That is acceptable for the schema. But when the event type has no destination calendar and the array holds only team members' calendars, the connected one will be wrong. Ordering is not guaranteed to put the organizer first.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent ignores the credentialId and always filters by the first destination
findings.body: The CalDAV base service takes `event.destinationCalendar[0]` and filters calendars by its externalId. For a collective event with multiple hosts on CalDAV credentials, each host's credential filters by the main host's calendar URL, so events are created in the wrong or no calendar. The `credentialId` argument is ignored, unlike the Google service.

findings.title: Office365 and Lark services ignore credentialId and use the first destination
findings.body: Both services pick the first destination calendar regardless of which credential is creating the event. For multi-host collective events, a second host's O365/Lark credential will attempt to write into the first host's calendar id, which fails or creates the event in the wrong place.

findings.title: E2E expectations inconsistent and no tests added
findings.body: Only the BOOKING_REJECTED expectation was updated to `[]`. BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect `destinationCalendar: null`. This works only because handleNewBooking can emit null, but it is inconsistent with the other handlers. The PR also adds no unit tests for the new multi-destination logic in EventManager, which is the core behavior change.
